question.problem:
Consider the function $f:R\to {R}^{3},$ defined by 

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}x \\ {x}^{2} \\ {x}^{3}\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the total derivative of $f$ with respect to $x?$
question.worked_solution:
The total derivative of a vector-valued function $f:R\to {R}^{m}$ with respect to a scalar $x$ is the column vector

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} \\ ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂x}\end{aligned}]\in {R}^{m\times 1}.
$$

In our case, the function 

- acts on a scalar $x\in R,$ and

- outputs a vector $f(x)\in {R}^{3}$ defined by 

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}x \\ {x}^{2} \\ {x}^{3}\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂x}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(x) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2x \\ 3{x}^{2}\end{aligned}]\in {R}^{3\times 1}.\end{aligned}
$$
